recentItems.title: True Blue (Troppo Azzurro) | One Summer, Two Loves | Full Romantic Comedy 4K
recentItems.description:
Watch the complete 4K presentation of True Blue (Troppo Azzurro), a tender Italian romantic comedy about the surprising complications of growing up. This film joins our digital cinema collection, featuring the 2024 theatrical release from director Filippo Barbagallo.

Written and directed by Filippo Barbagallo, who also plays Dario, the film is an Italian romantic comedy with a coming-of-age perspective. Its distinctive focus is the summer when a familiar life begins to change. Instead of relying on sensational events, the story builds on the contrast between emotional safety and a new connection. Barbagallo’s debut feature was presented at the Rome Film Fest in 2023 before its Italian cinema release in May 2024. The original screenplay and the film’s intimate approach place personal uncertainty at the heart of its comedy.

Dario is twenty-five and still living with his parents in Rome. He has kept the same circle of friends since high school and has settled into a life that feels reassuringly familiar. During a particularly hot August, he meets Caterina by chance and begins spending time with her. Then Lara, the seemingly unattainable girl he has loved for years, becomes another romantic possibility. With two relationships drawing him in different directions, Dario has to confront a choice he has long avoided: stay within his comfort zone or accept the risks of changing his life. The film follows that emotional crossroads without revealing how he resolves it.

Alongside Barbagallo, Alice Benvenuti plays Caterina and Martina Gatti plays Lara. Brando Pacitto appears as Sandro, with Valeria Milillo as Paola and Valerio Mastandrea as Franco. Their roles contribute to a portrait of a young man surrounded by people and expectations while still struggling to understand his own wishes. One of the central ideas is Dario’s uneasy relationship with change.

If you enjoy understated romantic comedies that find their biggest turning points in small decisions, this film offers a warm and recognisable perspective. Subscribe for more complete international cinema and character-led stories.
